title: Metrics Sculptor: tenant-aware OTel->Prometheus mapping and adaptive rollups
creator: Claire Zheng
description: Problem: Our hosted and dedicated customers emit high-cardinality inference telemetry (model_id, tenant_id, route, prompt_signature) that results in Prometheus label explosion and inconsistent KPIs across tenants. Existing ingestion creates too many series and unevenly distributed ingestion cost. Goal: implement a tenant-aware mapping layer ("Metrics Sculptor") that converts incoming OTel metrics into stable Prometheus-compatible series via configurable rollup policies and hot-key mitigation, while preserving the fidelity needed for SLIs.
design_summary: Metrics Sculptor is an ingestion-time transformation that sits in the OTel pipeline prior to Prometheus adapter. It will: 1) apply tenant-configurable cardinality policies (allow-listing keys, bucketing rules for string labels, numeric histogram bucketing), 2) perform prefix/KV caching-aware series coalescing to avoid kv-narrowing explosion, 3) detect hot keys and apply adaptive sampling/aggregation per-tenant, and 4) emit metadata markers to allow downstream reconstruction for debug mode. The layer is implemented as a horizontally scalable microservice in the telemetry fabric, with a lightweight rule engine backed by a per-tenant rulestore (config via Console).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end E2E: OTel metric for token_latency with tenant_id and model_id reduces unique Prometheus series by >=70% for top 10 tenants compared to baseline
No regression: P50/P95/P99 latency SLOs for inference RPCs must remain within 2% of baseline after rollout
Observability: Grafana dashboards show before/after series counts, dropped labels, and hot-key detection events
Rollback: Feature flag gating and per-tenant opt-out available via Console and env toggles
Integration tests: unit and integration tests for rule application, hot-key detection, and metadata passthrough exist in CI
implementation_steps: Prototype rule engine as sidecar to collector -> done (prototype branch)
Design tenant rule schema and Console UI hooks -> in review (spec: confluence.redwood.com/obs/metrics-sculptor-schema)
Add hot-key detector using reservoir sampling + sliding window counters -> PR #8456
Implement Prometheus adapter changes to accept transformed telemetry -> TODO
Load test in staging with synthetic high-cardinality workload -> TODO
Gradual rollout: canary 5 tenants -> 25 -> 100 with monitoring gates -> TODO
tradeoffs_and_risks: Cost vs fidelity: aggressive rollups reduce series but may hide tenant-specific regressions; mitigated by debug-mode passthrough and rerunnable ingests
Operational complexity: per-tenant rulestore adds config surface; mitigated with sane defaults and Console templates
Latency: additional transformation layer could add ~2-6ms p99 on pipeline path; we target <5ms median and provide async path for non-critical telemetry
Consistency: transformed labels make cross-tenant aggregation harder; record mapping metadata to enable selective rehydration
testing_plan: Unit tests for bucketing rules and label coalescing
Integration tests with collector -> adapter -> Prometheus in k8s test harness
Staging soak with 72h of synthetic inference traffic (mix of small and large tenants)
Comparison job that runs baseline ingestion in parallel to measure series delta and KPI divergence
monitoring_and_rollout_gates: Series reduction target per-tenant (>=60% for large tenants)
No more than 2% increase in telemetry pipeline latency
Error rate for telemetry ingress (drops/rejections) under 0.05%
Manual approval after canary metrics validated
